final_message:
I've saved the June 2026 draft for ABC Inc, with the commentary filled in, to `evals/runs/v4-run-20261013/e_abc_dec2025_one_offs/skill_output/`:
- `abc-inc-2026-06-trends.md` is the report.
- `abc-inc-2026-06-trends.json` holds every figure the script computed.

**Data quality:** all six checks pass, with no mismatches. That covers the subtotals, gross profit, operating income, net income, and assets against liabilities plus equity. June isn't flagged as a partial month. The export covers 18 months (Jan 2025 – Jun 2026), so the trailing-twelve-month (TTM) and same-month-last-year comparisons are all available.

**Main points from the commentary:**
- **Revenue:** 195,898, which is −6.0% against May 2026. May (208,351) was the highest month in the export, so the drop is measured from a peak. June is −0.5% against the prior 6-month average and +2.8% against June 2025.
- **Net income:** −330,756, the sixth negative month in a row; the TTM total is −3,089,780. December 2025 is the only positive month, and only because of non-operating items. Without them it would be −715,902; the largest is an Income Tax Benefit of −1,244,430.
- **Cash:** 713,481, down 215,543 from May and down 1,871,836 from six months earlier. Liabilities rose from 747,583 to 1,002,176.
- **December 2025 items:** stock-based compensation (334,661), a bonus (80,343) and the income tax benefit each appear to be single-month items. All three fall inside the TTM window, so they're included in the TTM figures. The reviewer should decide how to treat them.

The commentary also covers:
- Gross margin is 70.2% (+3.1 pp on May, −4.2 pp on June 2025).
- The Bad Debts line went negative (−1,806).
- Several revenue streams and expense lines are zero. Each is worded as something for the reviewer to confirm, not as a line that has stopped for good.

**"Other" category:** one account, General Expenses (149 in June, 16,158 TTM), matched no category rule.

This output folder belongs to the eval case `e_abc_dec2025_one_offs`, whose name suggests December 2025, but you asked for June 2026. June 2026 is also the latest month in the workbook, which is what the script reports on, so I produced June. If this case was meant to report on December 2025, that's worth checking.
